name: agent-builder-optional-release-agent
body:
The distributed `agent-builder` agent template `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md` (product source embedded into the `apg` binary via `include_str!` and installed by `apg init` into `~/.opencode/agents/`) must be able to scaffold an OPTIONAL, per-repo `release-agent` — the slot the removed optional `coordinator` vacated. Unlike the distributed suite agents, the `release-agent` is GENERATED per repo, never distributed: it needs repo-specific release-artefact write grants and the repo's remote/branch conventions, interviewed per repo exactly like the build gates.

Its shape: `mode: subagent`, `hidden: true`, `generated: true`; no `question` (it routes questions through the coordinator); it never actions Feedback — it returns an ACTIONED/WONT-FIX claim like every generated agent. It is grant-unusual in exactly one way: it is the ONLY generated agent granted `git push *` and `git tag *`, and its grant is `ask` — every push/tag command prompts for explicit human approval. Every OTHER generated agent gets no push/tag grant at all (denied by deny-by-default).

Release-artefact write scope (amended by `requirements.requirement.code-writer-worktree-only-writes`): releases are made from MAIN, so the release-agent's write grants target the MAIN checkout — it is one of the two agent carve-outs of `global.constraint.worktree-isolation` and needs no `apg/.worktrees/*/` mirror. Its main-write set is REPO-SPECIFIC and is never a fixed list: the agent-builder ANALYSES the repo (what its release touches — e.g. version files, packaging formulae, changelog, release scripts) and RECOMMENDS the set, which is confirmed through the coordinator interview exactly like build gates and test tiers. The spec fixes only this policy; no release-artefact path list is a law.

The `release-agent` performs the repo's release: it is granted the release-adjacent git ops (tagging and pushing the branch and tags) plus write access to that per-repo release-artefact set on main. The `codebase-navigator` dispatches it through the `task` tool ONLY after obtaining **explicit user consent**, and the grant is `ask`, so approval surfaces both at dispatch and per command.

This is a deliberate CARVE-OUT of the repo's recurring "push/tag remain human-approved acts" rule (the scoped law is `requirements.constraint.push-tag-release-agent-carve-out`, restated by `requirements.requirement.push-tag-human-approved-release-only`): the rule continues to bind every other agent and path; only the deliberately-invoked release-agent is exempt, and only behind the consent gate and the per-op `ask`.

The carve-out is an AGENT-policy statement, NOT a binary one. The `apg` binary still never pushes or tags: it is git2-only (`default-features = false`; the git CLI is never shelled out to) and `scripts/release.sh` itself still never pushes — the release-agent may run it and then push/tag itself. The wording of that binary-policy statement on the binary-doc surfaces is corrected from "human acts" to "human-approved acts" by `requirements.requirement.push-tag-human-approved-release-only`; the binary's behaviour is unchanged.

Surfaces to edit (all real `docs` File nodes in the branch graph):
- `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md` — the optional `release-agent` in the generated set (roster intro, `### release-agent (optional)` section, workflow interview bullet, step-4/step-5 scaffold) and its grant shape (push/tag `ask`; main-checkout release-artefact edits derived per repo by analysis + interview; no worktree mirror); push/tag prose states ONLY the release-agent is granted push/tag, as `ask`.
- `opencode-suite/agents/codebase-navigator.md` — explicit user consent BEFORE tasking the release-agent; `release-agent` in its `task` allowlist; human-approved push/tag phrasing.
- `AGENTS.md` — the optional release-agent, the consent gate, the release-agent-only push/tag rule, its per-repo main-write scope, and the human-approved phrasing.

Acceptance criteria:
- `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md` offers and scaffolds the optional per-repo `release-agent`: `mode: subagent`, `hidden: true`, `generated: true`, no `question`, returning ACTIONED/WONT-FIX claims; it is the ONLY generated agent granted push/tag, as `ask`; every other generated agent carries no push/tag grant.
- The template instructs the agent-builder to derive the release-agent's main-checkout write set by analysing the repo and to confirm it via the coordinator interview; it hardcodes no release-artefact path list as a rule, and grants no worktree mirror for it.
- `opencode-suite/agents/codebase-navigator.md` states the navigator obtains explicit user consent BEFORE dispatching the release-agent, and its `task` allowlist contains `release-agent`.
- `AGENTS.md` documents the release-agent, the consent gate, the release-agent-only push/tag rule, its per-repo main-write scope and the human-approved phrasing.
- The binary's git2-only behaviour is unchanged.
- Scope is product source + the repo guide only; the repo's own `.opencode/agents/**` are consumer artifacts and are NOT edited.
